### Task 11.289 — 2026-09-20 — commit bfc7631 — Done

**Closed 2026-09-20 on Michael's device look**, reported in the same window: *"1 and 2 tested and
verified"* — a published project deleted with signal reached the server as a tombstone, and one
deleted in airplane mode reached it after the network came back. The plan's `Status` is `Done` and
the command file is deleted in the same commit. **Item 3 below (his nine stranded rows) is still
his to check** and is not part of the acceptance; task 11.290 is now unblocked. The entry as first
written follows.


**What changed, in one sentence:** a project you delete on the phone now reaches the server as a
deletion — including when you delete it with no signal and get signal back days later — where
before it stayed live on the server forever and came back on every new device.

**Why it never arrived.** The app syncs one project at a time: the one you have open. Deleting the
open project clears "which project is open", and a deleted project is hidden from the list so it
can never be opened again. So the deletion sat on the phone, marked as waiting, with nothing that
would ever send it. Selecting another project sends *that* project's records. The project's own
row is the only record in the app whose deletion removes the very thing that would have sent it.
(Task 11.57 met the same trap for leaving a project; this is that fix, for deleting one.)

**What was built.** `pending_project_change.dart` finds, from the data, every project whose own
row has a change the server has not confirmed — a deletion, an undo, a rename from the list — on
a project the server knows about. `SyncController.deliverPendingProjectChanges` sends one round
for each. It runs on every app open and every return to the foreground (the durable path), when
you tap "Sync now", and immediately after Delete or UNDO on the Projects list (an attempt; it
fails quietly with no signal and the foreground hook carries on). Which rows a phone may send at
all is asked of the sync engine's own rule (`SyncEngine.wouldOffer`), not copied — so a departed
member's or a snapshot holder's local delete is still never sent.

**What the change costs, in writing.** Ordinary sync is still one project at a time; nothing about
the status icon, the counts, or the per-project bookmarks changed. Added: on each app open or
foreground, one read of the projects table plus one small local query per project the server
knows about; no network at all unless a project row is stranded, and then one push-and-pull for
that project only, until the server confirms it. "Sync now" may take one extra round trip when
something is stranded. The alternative — sync every project every round — was rejected: it
multiplies network traffic by the number of projects on a phone on cellular, and the status
surface would have to describe all of them at once.

**Michael's nine live projects, addressed.** Every project he deleted *on this phone* will be
repaired from the app on its own: the deleted rows are still on the phone, still linked (only
leaving a project unlinks it; signing out does not), and the first app open of this build with
signal sends each one. The app cannot repair a project deleted on a device he no longer has, or
one the server refuses — those would need an operator `UPDATE ... SET deleted_at` on the VM, and
step 3 below is how to tell which are which. Not all nine are deletions; his real projects are in
that count too.

**The server half, which his measurement never reached** because the phone never made the push:
`publish_and_join_test.dart` now pushes an owner's project tombstone weeks after the fact and
confirms `deleted_at` is stored and `/projects/mine` no longer lists it; a contributor's tombstone
for the owner's project is refused.

**Watched red first** on the manual "Sync now" path (with no project open, and with another
project open) — Michael's exact steps — and on the screen's Delete control.

   instrument.** The request count is the fact that matters and it is now proven exactly; the

   Michael's wifi would not predict a phone on LTE in the field. **F1 is itself a field measurement,

### Task 11.281 — 2026-09-18 — commit 06af81b — Done

**In one sentence:** the map's cold-cache terrain fetch now issues 143 terrarium-tile requests for
the seeded 35 km viewshed where it issued 380, and the Offline Data Map's DEM download job got the
identical fix for free.

**What changed.** `DemTileFetcher.fetchTile` (`lib/viewshed/dem_tile_fetcher.dart`) takes an
optional `TerrainTileCache` — a thin `z/x/y`-keyed lookup, checked before each terrarium-tile fetch
and filled in as new ones arrive — instead of starting from an empty map on every call.
`_ensureTerrainForRegion` in `map_screen.dart` (the viewshed's auto-terrain path) creates one before
its loop over a region's DEM tiles and shares it across every `fetchTile` call in that loop. Scoped
to one region fill, per the brief: `DemTileStore` already persists DEM tiles across fills, and
`/w-20`'s measured redundancy was entirely inside one fill, at the terrarium layer.

**Discovered scope, applied rather than filed:** `DownloadManager._runDem` (the Offline Data Map's
DEM download job) has the identical loop-over-DEM-tiles shape and pays the identical redundancy on
any job covering more than one DEM tile. Since the fix is the same `TerrainTileCache` with no new
abstraction, it got the same one-line treatment in this task rather than a separate number.

**Regression test:** `test/viewshed/dem_tile_fetcher_test.dart`, group "region fill (task 11.281)".
Reproduces `_ensureTerrainForRegion`'s own bounds computation for the seeded fixture (`seedLat`
42.7008, `seedLon` -117.3612, 35 km range) — without importing `map_screen.dart` — confirms it
yields the same 72 DEM tiles `/w-20` measured, then asserts 143 terrarium-tile requests with a
shared cache and 380 without one. Both numbers matched `/w-20`'s real-bucket measurement exactly on
the first run.

it runs without network access. Applying `/w-20`'s measured mean (125–133 ms/request) to 143
requests instead of 380 projects to roughly 18–19 s instead of ~50–53 s on the same connection —
stated as a projection from `/w-20`'s numbers, not a new measurement.

### Task 11.280 — resolved 2026-09-18 by the planning session

**`Done`, and it is the best task on the board this month: it refused the brief's question, asked a
better one, and found a defect nobody had reported in three weeks of daily use.**

1. **My fork was wrong and the correction is now a rule.** The brief offered *“real slow-down”* or
   *“always-slow path”* — both of which assume the state was never produced. **It was produced,
   correctly, instantly, and then undone on the next screen build.** No number of twenty-second runs
   distinguishes those; one `print` at the classification site settled it in one run. **When a
   readiness condition times out on a state something is supposed to reach, instrument the producer
   before forking on fast-versus-slow** — “did it happen at all” comes before “how long did it
   take”. Added to `CLAUDE.md`.

2. **The defect is far bigger than the screenshot, and it is a §4.27 defeat.** Any owner who left or
   was removed from a project they created had their membership **silently re-inserted by their own
   device** on the next screen build, forever, and would never learn from the app that their access
   had ended. The server was answering correctly the whole time; the device threw the answer away.
   **Written into `TriTrack_Security_Model.md` beside §4.27** as a `Fixed 2026-09-18` paragraph —
   the answer to item 2's question is yes, that document does track fixed issues in exactly that
   form (see *“Fixed: prior email addresses”*).

3. **Item 3 is recorded, not re-derived.** Contributors and viewers were never affected — the repair
   keys on `Projects.owner_user_id`. In the security model beside the rest.

4. **Deliberately not dated, and that was right.** It has presumably been true since whichever of
   8.4/11.1 and 11.54/11.60 landed second. **A date written from inference is the kind of number this
   project has been wrong about four times**, and the fix does not depend on it.

5. **The escape hatch was mine again — the third break of the same test, in a third way.**
   `/w-20`'s command file had `description: "/w-20 — …"`; the check reads the id with
   `RegExp(r'Task\s+/?`?(\d+\.\d+|w-\d+)')`, so the description named **no task at all** and
   disagreed with the filename. **Fixed — the description now reads `Task /w-20 — …`, the house
   format the deleted `/w-19` file used.** Three breaks of one guard, in three different ways, is
   not three mistakes; it is one missing step. **`CLAUDE.md` now says to run
   `command_file_staleness_test.dart` after writing any command file, before committing** — a rule
   telling me to be careful has now failed twice, and a command that takes two seconds has not been
   tried once.

6. **A picture that cannot be taken is a finding.** This defect existed for weeks with a server
   answering correctly, a device quietly overriding it, and nobody noticing — until a *screenshot*
   could not be captured. That is the strongest argument this project has yet produced for the
   screenshot lane costing what it costs.

**Nothing further to task from this.**

   build still refuses the same pair locally, is what keeps it honest. **Two tests, not prose**, for
   a give-up that would otherwise exist only in a comment.

### Task 11.270 — resolved 2026-09-17 by the planning session

**`Done`, nothing to task, and design §6b's noted limit is closed rather than widened.**

1. **The general finding is now a rule in `CLAUDE.md`, because it will happen again.** *A rule
   checked one row at a time cannot approve a change that is only valid as a pair.* The interlock
   was right about each half and wrong about the change, and no order of edits avoided it — which
   is this project's *refusal with no way forward is a trap*, manufactured out of a rule that is
   otherwise correct. **The fix was not to relax the rule**: `DeploymentLinking.applyHandover`
   checks it once against both rows' final values and writes both. The rule also carries the tell,
   so the next one is caught before it is a bug report — when a screen offers a correction that
   only makes sense on two rows at once, ask which invariant sees the halfway state.

2. **Four routes, one derivation — and that is the right answer, noted so it is not mistaken for
   under-scoping.** `_setAttached`'s overlap branch and both of `_setRemoved`'s forced-time branches
   all reach the deadlock, and all four share `bareDayHandoverPartner` rather than four copies of
   the question. That is the shape this project keeps asking for and rarely gets on the first try.

3. **Michael's field-facing summary is exact and needs no translation**: if "this animal would be
   wearing two tags at once" ever appeared while correcting one collar's date right after fixing the
   other's to the same day, that specific dead end is gone — one dialog naming both collars and one
   time, and confirming writes both.

**No command files to write.**

**Both `Done`. The hypothesis held, the audit went where it was told to go, and the class of defect

   it as the precedent it is: when a test's failure and a production function are both candidates,
   the question of which one is wrong is answered before either is touched, because fixing the test
   is what makes the question unaskable.**

### Task 11.275 — resolved 2026-09-17 by the planning session

**The instrument works, the finding is real, and one sentence of the write-up is overstated — which
matters, because that sentence is what the next task would have acted on.**

1. **Urgency: not urgent, and 11.276 goes next anyway.** Nothing is red on any machine anyone uses,
   and CI does not return until 1 October, so neither defect is blocking field work or a release.
   But 11.276 has a question inside it that gets harder to ask the longer it waits, so it is next in
   the queue regardless of its urgency. **11.277 runs first, in the same window** — both need the
   same slow three-zone verification runs, and a window holding two unrelated reds cannot tell which
   fix cleared which. Two windows both running `flutter test` on one machine is the exact condition
   task 11.253 could not reproduce and would not rule out.

2. **“Two independent bugs are cancelling to a false green” overstates it, and 11.276's entry has
   been amended.** The planning session read `deployment_interlock.dart` and grepped `lib/`,
   `server/lib/` and `packages/*/lib/`: **every production write of a deployment date goes through
   `deploymentDateFor(DateTime.now())`, which yields local midnight, and no production code anywhere
   builds a deployment date as `DateTime.utc(y, m, d)`.** The only such literals outside `test/` are
   `_comparisonStamp`, two WMM year boundaries and two `plausibleFloor` constants.

   So `deploymentDateFor` looks exact for every value a device actually writes, and what it misreads
   is a value written in another zone — which is the cross-zone gap its own class comment documents
   at length, the plan already carries in Discovered Scope, and task 11.263 already gave a second
   reader. **A documented deferred gap is not a second bug**, and calling it one would have sent
   11.276 to change a production date function on the strength of a test fixture.

   **This reading is a hypothesis, not a finding**, and 11.276's amended item 1 says so: its job is
   to confirm or overturn it in writing, before any fixture is edited, because making the ten tests
   green erases the only evidence the question was ever askable.

3. **What is worth keeping from this that the write-up did not name:** under Arizona a fixture's
   `DateTime.utc(y, m, d)` is not local midnight, so `deploymentEndHasTime` reads it as a *time*.
   **Those ten tests have been exercising the server's reading of a deployment date, not a
   device's**, for as long as they have existed, while reading on the page as though they proved
   device behaviour. That is now item 2 of 11.276.

4. **The fixtures should build a bare day through `deploymentDateFor`, not with a second literal.**
   A hand-maintained copy of a derivation is already wrong — this project's own rule — and a second
   literal is precisely how this fixture family drifted from production's definition of a day.

5. **The scope fence holds.** No further timezone sweep of the suite as part of 11.276. Task 11.275
   found what it found; anything beyond it is a task with its own evidence.

**Command files written 2026-09-17:** `/11-277` and `/11-276` (neither existed when the tasks were
filed — Michael found this by trying to run one).

### Task 11.271 — resolved 2026-09-17 by the planning session

**`Done`, and it scoped itself exactly where its brief told it to — which is right, and leaves the
promoted question open.**

1. **The narrow scope is compliance, not a shortfall.** The brief said *"do not parameterise every
   test by timezone… scope it, and say how you scoped it."* **It scoped it to one file's
   date-boundary logic and said so.** Its item 1 is also the correct framing: **`main`'s green now has
   two layers and neither replaces the other.**
2. **But the sentence that got this task promoted is still true**, and it is being named rather than
   quietly treated as closed: *"nobody currently knows whether `main` is green — only that it is
   green at the times somebody happened to run it."* **A harness over one file does not close that**,
   and the task never claimed it did.
3. **Task 11.275 closes it, and it is the cheapest instrument on the list because it changes no
   tests at all.** Every defect in this class turns on **how far the wall clock is from local
   midnight** — and that distance is a function of the **process time zone**. **So run the existing
   suite unchanged under three `TZ` values** and you sample three distances from midnight at the same
   moment. **Nothing in `test/` changes.**
4. **It has to prove the instrument before trusting it**, which is this project's own rule applied to
   a new tool: **reproduce a known time-of-day defect by `TZ` alone, against its pre-fix commit.** If
   `TZ` cannot surface one we already know is clock-dependent, **the instrument does not work and
   that is the finding**, not a footnote.
5. **Its item 2 is left exactly as it wrote it.** `observation_logging_screen.dart` reads the
   unfixed clock and has the same shape; **nothing has broken there yet**, and the brief told it not
   to widen. **11.275 must not fold it in either** — if the zone sweep surfaces a defect there, that
   is evidence and it gets its own task; if not, 11.271's trigger stands as written.
6. **Three instruments, three questions, and the entry makes them say so in `README.md`:**
   repetition samples load and ordering; the clock matrix samples one file's date logic; the zone
   sweep samples the whole suite's distance from midnight. **None of them is the others**, and a
   project that has now spent three evenings on this class should not have to rediscover which tool
   answers which question.

   too: the Map's legend will gain a row for an animal that no longer exists, **and that is correct**,
   because the legend describes what is drawn.

### Tasks 11.269 and 11.268 — resolved 2026-09-17 by the planning session

**Both `Done`, and between them they corrected the planning session twice and found a gap in an
instrument this project already trusts.**

1. **`main`'s red was task 11.264's own commit, and 11.264's green was real.** The defect is a
   **timezone** bug — `_setAttached` handed the date picker a stored UTC instant where it needed the
   local calendar day, while `_setRemoved` beside it already converted — **so the test is true only
   some hours of the day in a UTC-negative zone.** "Either it went red later or the green was wrong"
   had a third answer neither of us offered: **the green was right and not reproducible.**
2. **Worth sitting with: that is the class task 11.264 was sweeping for — day versus instant — and
   the sweep introduced one while removing four.** Not an argument against sweeping. **An argument
   for the rule that a task's own diff is the last place it looks.**
3. **A second red the same evening was the same shape** — a fixture seeding *"two hours from now"*
   and assuming that stays on today's date, false within two hours of local midnight. **Two of two.**
4. **Which opens a gap in task 11.253, and it is task 11.271, above the line.** 11.253 ran the suite
   ten times and closed; its entry records that the ten runs *"removed the one variable that
   separates the two conditions"* — **and I meant machine load. Nobody named the clock.** **Ten runs
   in one quiet evening sample one moment of the day**, so a test that fails only near local midnight
   **passes ten out of ten at 9pm**, and `repeat_suite.sh` says so with a straight face. **The
   protocol is not wrong; its denominator counts the wrong thing.**
5. **Task 11.268 refused item 6's mechanism and was right — the precedent I gave it does not
   transfer.** I said retire `pulse_pattern` as `TagColumnKind.retired`, the way `Tags.color_hex`
   was. **`color_hex` was `display` and had never been on `Tag_Versions`; `pulse_pattern` has been
   `measurementContext` since schema v9 and is already on every version row**, because
   `versionedTagColumnNames` derives the physical schema from that same classification.
   **Reclassifying would derive the column off a table the migrations still build** — a mismatch only
   a migration fixes, which is the schema-major bump my own first bullet forbade. **The kind stays;
   only the form field goes.** **The general rule is now written in both places it will be looked
   for:** `retired` is a precedent for a `display`-kind column, and **retiring a versioned column is
   a migration, not a reclassification.**
6. **And its item 2 is a defect a test caught before it shipped, which is the system working.**
   Writing `pulsePattern: null` unconditionally manufactured a spurious *"was steady, becomes —"*
   row in the tag edit-intent dialog on **any** edit — including a pure colour change, which that
   dialog's own rule says must ask nothing. Carried the existing value forward instead.
7. **Two derivation guards needed their tracked numbers moved, not their logic** — and **both caught
   exactly what they exist to catch.** Nothing owed.
8. **Nothing owed by Michael on either task.**

   overlap by editing them one after another** — proven by working `DeploymentInterlock.overlaps`'
   arithmetic through, not guessed. This is not a defect in what shipped — the control asked for
   exists, matching the acceptance — but §6b reads as promising full resolution and doesn't quite. Ask
   whether the design doc should say so, or whether a follow-up (e.g. a coordinated two-row edit,

### Task 11.264 — resolved 2026-09-17 by the planning session

**`Done`, and it justified being a sweep rather than a fix: 24 decisions derived, 18 still right with
the reason written beside each, 2 fixed, 2 bigger, 2 stale sentences.** Two of the four wrong ones
were created by task 11.263 **three days after the rule it implemented was written** — which is the
argument for sweeping rather than waiting for a phone.

1. **Item 1 is the finding the sweep existed for, and the answer is: offer the time, never prefill
   it. Design §6b, task 11.265.** A handover that happened on the 10th and is entered on the 12th
   **cannot be recorded at all**, and the refusal names an action no control offers — *a refusal with
   no way forward*, which this project already calls a trap.
   **§6a's justification was mine and it was too narrow:** *"a past-day removal cannot overlap with
   today in any case"* — true, and it looked only at *today*, while the pair it overlaps is on that
   past day. **§4b is narrowed rather than reversed**, on one distinction: **asking is not inventing;
   prefilling is.** An empty picker asks the person who was there for a fact they hold. **Refusing to
   record what happened puts the data at *absent* rather than *approximate*, and approximate and
   recorded beats exact and missing.**
2. **Item 2 is task 11.266, and the flag is chosen over the column — with the price corrected.** The
   doc says *one minute in 1 440*; **11.264 is right that hand-picked times cluster on whole hours,
   so it is one in 24**, and 5 p.m. is a plausible hour to take a collar off. **A number that makes a
   defect look negligible is worse than no number**, and the entry requires the doc corrected.
   **The column stays open and unbundled**: it is §4's cross-zone *display* problem, a different
   question, and closing it inside a server fix would bury it.
3. **Item 3's stale sentences are amended — the doc is mine and they were mine.** §5a's *"a zero-day
   overlap, comfortably inside §6's one-day allowance"* described an allowance that no longer exists;
   §6a's and §4b's are the reasoning item 1 orphaned, and both are struck with the reason rather than
   rewritten silently.
4. **Item 4's answer — no instrument, on purpose — is accepted, and the reasoning is the good part.**
   *"The right and wrong uses of a day comparison are the same expression; only the justifying
   sentence differs, and a test cannot read that."* **That is a real finding**, and better than a
   guard that fires on every date comparison. **The trip-wire it left instead is the right shape:**
   three readers compare dates on their own today, each with a written reason — **a fourth buys an
   allowlist test.** A threshold with a reader, unlike the one task 11.236 left.
5. **Item 5 is the first time a task applied 11.253's rule properly without being told to.** It found
   a flaky test of 11.263's, **reproduced it 2 in 7**, checked explicitly that nothing else was
   running and no `.git` lock was held, fixed the actual cause — a time floor taken after the tap

### Task 11.263 — 2026-09-16 — commit ac1cfb4 — Done

**The one-day overlap allowance is withdrawn. The shared interlock now refuses two deployments that
share any moment — read the same way a bearing is attributed: a bare day covers its whole day, a time
is an instant. Watched red against the old body on a same-day handover recorded as two bare days;
green on a timed one. The Record screen's handover prompt (11.260) and collar chooser (11.262) are
deleted, and `untimedHandoverFor` with them (its only readers were the prompt and its tests).
`writeRemovedDate` stays. Fold back at 186 logical pixels with and without a legacy pair present,
wheel rows at 3. Both suites green locally: app 3468 passed / 15 skipped; server 62 of 62 suites,
1030 tests, 0 skipped. No CI.**

**Two defects in the server's enforcement, found because this is the first server test that ever
pushed a swap, both fixed in this commit:**

- **The server refused the ordinary same-day swap on every sync since 2026-09-14.** `applyPush`
  decides every row against the *stored* rows and writes afterwards, so the new deployment in a swap
  was checked against the old one still open in the store — an unbounded overlap — and held on the
  device as "the server would not take this". Now each deployment row is checked against the store
  as the earlier rows in the page leave it (the device pushes in the order it wrote them).
- **A withdrawal was refused if the row being withdrawn overlapped anything.** The rule skipped a
  stored tombstone and never asked whether the arriving row was one. A tombstone now conflicts with
  nothing in either position.

**For the planning session**

1. **§4a's "Where the time is offered" paragraph lists two shapes; the code now has three.** The link
   confirmation also offers a time when the animal's *previous* collar came off earlier today on her
   own screen (nothing to close, no history on the new collar). Without it, Michael's ordinary
   two-step — collar 1 off Kea with a time, collar 2 on — was a bare-day link overlapping the
   morning, refused. Add the third shape to §4a.
2. **A decision to put to Michael, with its number (Discovered Scope has the long form).** *Day only*
   is withheld exactly where it would overlap, as briefed — but a removal recorded today as a bare
   day when nothing overlaps *yet* makes that collar unlinkable to anyone for the rest of the day,
   and the other animal's picker hides it without saying why. That is his own tag-2 flow of
   2026-09-15. The smaller remedy is to withhold *Day only* for *today* altogether (a time defaulted
   to now is a tap; the design keeps *Day only* for a *past* day). Ask him, or decide.
3. **§4a's cross-zone reopen trigger now has a second reader: the server.** It reads the bare-day
   sentinel in its own zone (UTC in the container), so a bare day written in Arizona reads there as
   07:00 — narrower — and a timed swap that lands on exactly 17:00:00 Arizona reads as a UTC bare day
   — wider, and would be refused on push. Priced on `DeploymentInterlock`'s doc comment (one minute
   in 1 440 for a hand-picked time). The nullable instant column or a stored zone closes both. Amend
   the trigger's wording to name the server, and consider whether 11.264 owns the column.
4. **§4a says the reopen triggers are named "on `deploymentEndHasTime` in `deployment.dart`".** Both
   sentinel functions moved to `packages/tritrack_sync/lib/src/deployment_interlock.dart` (the
   interlock needs them); the app re-exports them with a forwarding note. Move the pointer.
5. **Task 11.264's brief should know:** the vocabulary this task left behind is in comments only
   (`zero-day`, `one-day allowance`, `more than a day`) and every occurrence I touched is rewritten;
   `grep -rn "one-day\|zero-day\|more than a day" lib packages server test` on 2026-09-16 finds only
   historical sentences that say "until task 11.263". A season clone of a project holding a legacy
   bare-day pair is refused with the interlock sentence — that is the rule working, and
   `new_season_screen.dart` says so.

### Task 11.262 — resolved 2026-09-16, and superseded the same day by Michael's push-back

**`Done` and tested — and then Michael rejected the machinery rather than its wording, and he is
right.** His report: the line reads *"<Animal Name> has <n> collars removed today - which one?"*,
*"This isn't clear. I'm realizing we may be over complicating this."*

1. **The wording was not the problem and rewording it would have been the wrong fix.** **The
   ambiguity itself is avoidable**, and everything built to explain it — task 11.260's prompt, this
   task's chooser — exists downstream of **one tolerance nobody re-read**: §6's one-day overlap
   allowance, which was the only way to record a handover when a deployment knew nothing finer than
   a calendar day. **Task 11.251 made a handover an overlap of zero.** The tolerance now survives
   only as the route by which *Day only* creates the state.
2. **Design §6a withdraws it**, and **task 11.263 implements the withdrawal by deleting code**: any
   overlap refused, once, in the shared package the server also enforces; *Day only* withheld
   exactly where it would overlap and kept where a time would be invented; **the prompt and the
   chooser removed, because the state they describe can no longer arise.**
3. **Michael's lockout idea is refused in writing, in §6a, with the reason.** Refusing at the source
   means the state cannot come from this build, so a lockout could only fire on legacy rows — and
   **locking a field crew out of recording, in the field, to fix a data-entry problem is a large
   hammer for a case pre-beta data makes nearly impossible.**
4. **§4a's contested answer survives and 11.263 must assert it still reachable.** It is the honest
   reply for a row from an older build and for the cross-zone case. **This app can no longer create
   one; that is not the same as it never existing.**
5. **Task 11.264 is the sweep, and it exists because this is the second withdrawal in three days.**
   The wheel's whole-day rule went first; the interlock's tolerance goes now. **Both existed because
   a deployment could not say when, both survived 11.251 unexamined, and both were found by a phone
   rather than by anything in the repository.** `CLAUDE.md` has the rule and **a rule with no
   instrument behind it is what let two through** — so 11.264 also has to answer whether anything
   cheap could have caught them, including *"no, and here is why"*.
6. **Nothing about 11.262's own work was wrong.** It did what it was asked. **The task it was asked
   to do should not have existed**, which is the planning session's finding and not its.

   run: a command file's blocker line is a claim, and claims go stale.** A header that says
   "do not run" while the plan says "run it after X" is two documents disagreeing about a case
   neither had seen — and the task was right to read both and say what it was doing.

   member may already read and writes only into a **new** project the person creates and owns, so
   nothing about their standing on the source can be widened. **A viewer may start next season from
   a project they may not edit**, and that is not escalation — the new project contains only what
   they could already see, and **the old project is not written at all.**

   bearings point at; the old chain stays beside the old bearings; a re-tuned collar next season is

   reader meets it**, which is the right place for it.

   which the task was right to separate from its own scope.** `removeFromProject` and
   `IndividualRepository.remove` each tombstone their own row and stop, so **a deployment outlives
   both of its foreign keys** and nobody has measured what the screens do with one. **The entry
   forbids working from a list of readers** — 11.251 found six where I had written four — and
   **refuses to assume cascading is right**, because a deployment records that this collar was on
   this animal between these dates and that stays true. It must answer explicitly what happens to a
   bearing whose animal resolves through a link to a deleted animal.

   call: the decision's *consequence* was unchanged and only its mechanism had been replaced by the

   not re-opening it.**

   **nothing drifted — every string is new, so `check_app_quotes` is silent on all of it.**

**What changed, in one sentence:** the New season screen has a second switch, *Bring over last
known positions*, on by default, which carries each copied animal's most recent position
estimate and most recent truth point into the new season so the crew can re-establish where
the animals are. Michael asked for it while reading the 11.56 report: *"it might be useful to

positions of the animals in the study… a slider in the dialog that defaults to on."*

**For the planning session**
1. **Two readings of "known truth positions" were possible and I built the narrower one — say
   if the other was meant.** I read it as *the last known position from either kind of
   record*, so it is one estimate and one truth point per animal, the most recent of each.
   The wider reading is *every* truth point of every copied animal (a nest, a carcass, a
   den — all of them). The engine is one condition away from the wider one; the
   `SeasonCloneDisposition.lastKnownPerAnimal` argument would need a second paragraph.
2. **Attribution is by deployment interval, and a collar on nobody at the time carries
   nothing.** An estimate for a collar that was on the shelf when it was computed, or on an
   animal that is not being copied, does not come across — tested. This is the app's own
   `animalForObservationIn`, so the same-day handover defect in Phase 12's Discovered Scope
   (2026-09-15) applies here too, and is fixed here when it is fixed there.
3. **Two columns are not carried as they were, and both are decisions rather than
   omissions.** A copied truth point's `user_id` (who found it) is kept only when that is the
   person cloning, because the server refuses any *new* row naming another user
   (`namesForeignUser`) and a copy naming last season's finder would be held on the phone
   forever. Its `tag_version_id` is cleared: it names a version in last season's chain, and
   pointing it at the new collar's first version would claim the point was recorded against a
   reading it was not. An estimate's `observation_ids_used` **is** carried — it is what the
   estimate came from, and the column is unvalidated by design — which means the Map's
   "N bearings used" line on a carried-over estimate counts bearings that live in last
   season's project, and tapping it highlights nothing. Said here so the first person to see
   that does not file it as a defect.

   positions* with its count line, and the "What stays" sentence now has two forms — with the
   switch on, *"…every position estimate and truth point except the most recent one for each
   animal."* `check_app_quotes`: still the same 9 pre-existing reds, none from this.

**For Michael**

**Both `Done`, both did the thing the brief asked for rather than the thing that would have looked

**The class is defined, derived from the code, and guarded — and it condemns nothing today.** The
"Cannot use the Ref … after it has been disposed" failure that broke the tag database's + button
(11.235) and Sync Status's "Try again" (11.236) needs three things at once: an auto-disposing
provider, a `ref` or `state` use after a completed `await`, and a read that nothing keeps alive.
`test/core/providers/ref_after_await_hazards_test.dart` measures that (ten cases, riverpod 3.3.2);
`test/core/providers/ref_after_await_guard_test.dart` derives the population on every run and fails
on a member with all three. **Today: 48 auto-disposing providers, 8 with the body shape, 19 reached by
a bare read, 0 condemned.** Watched red on the real tree twice — a bare read of
`snapshotProjectIdsProvider` added, and 11.236's `strandedRecordCount` fix reverted — and on fixtures
with known answers per verdict.

**For the planning session**
1. **The two hazards are two hazards, measured.** (a) The bare read: needs the three things above,
   and the bare read's `.future` completes with an error rather than hanging. (b) An invalidation
   landing mid-build: **independent of the body shape** — a bare `keepAlive` read never completes
   whether or not its body touches `ref` after a gap (nothing listens, so the rebuild is lazy and
   never runs; the stale value is discarded, silently), and the same invalidation is harmless to
   anything listened to. **So no predicate over provider bodies can find (b); it belongs to
   `ArrivalRefresh.settleFirst` (task 11.153), which already guards it.** The `currentUser` comment's
   "orphaned forever" is (b) self-inflicted and measures true for a bare read, false for a listened
   one — the comment stands. `tag_view_refresh.dart`'s comment was not edited either.
2. **11.238's exemption — "always watched, never read bare" — is complete for (a) and for (b).** But
   it is a fact about call sites, not about the provider, so the guard derives it rather than
   accepting it as a note: every `.read(` of an auto-disposing provider anywhere in `lib/`, followed
   transitively through what a bare-read auto-dispose provider watches, stopping at `keepAlive`
   (11.236's one-level-down finding is that transitive edge). The 8 shape-bearing providers are all
   "only ever watched", and `snapshotProjectIds` and `unsyncedMemberProjectIds` now carry a written
   statement of why that is safe, pointing at the guard.
3. **The count reconciled, and one sentence of 11.235's corrected.** 11.235's eleven, less the four
   11.236 fixed, plus 11.238's two, less `mayWriteProjectData` (which 11.236 found was never in
   shape) is eight — what the guard derives. 11.235 called `await ref.watch(x.future)` "the safe
   form"; **it is safe only with respect to its own `await`** — a second one after it runs after the
   first gap and is the shape, which is exactly what 11.236 fixed in `strandedRecordCount` and
   `serverHttpClient`. The guard's fixtures pin both readings.
4. **The predicate's blind spots, so they are known rather than discovered:** a helper that stores a
   `Ref` and uses it later, and a provider read through an alias or a variable, are invisible to a
   textual derivation. Exemptions are a map in the guard with a reason per entry, checked in both
   directions (a condemned member needs one; an entry whose member is no longer condemned fails).

   first.**

   read bare *and* invalidated mid-build was not measured here (11.153's comment says it throws

### Task 11.254 — resolved 2026-09-15 by the planning session

**It refuted the premise it was given, and it was right to.** My brief said a merge is an operation
every row of which is legal, and asked for an operation-level check. **The measurement says there is
no operation:** a contributor can produce a merge's exact end state with four ordinary buttons —
withdraw each collar, attach it to the other animal, edit the attached date back, *Delete animal* —
so the owner rung on *"Same animal as…"* is **a rung on one button**, and **a server cannot refuse a
distinction the product does not make.** That sentence is the whole finding and it was not in the
brief.

1. **Michael chose option (a) the same day: *"I like the idea of deleting an animal is an own only
   decision."*** It is **task 11.255**, above the line for Gate C, with a command file.
2. **The rung goes on destruction, which is the distinction the product does make.** Re-pointing
   collars is recoverable by hand; a deleted animal is not. **Both routes close at the same
   control.**
3. **It half-reverses task 11.244, and 11.244's reason survives — which is why the reversal is safe.**
   11.244 said a contributor may remove an animal made by mistake. **A contributor can still rename
   it and withdraw its collars**, and neither destroys a record. **A mistake stays fixable by the
   person who made it; what moves behind the owner rung is destroying a record, not correcting one.**
   11.255 requires the screen to say that when it refuses — a refusal that names only what you cannot
   do is the thing tasks 11.220/11.221 were written against. 11.244's entry carries the amendment.
4. **`MutationRule` cannot express this and that is recorded rather than worked around.** One rule
   per table, no delete/update distinction — so 11.255 is a `RowAuthorizer` branch mirroring
   `_authorizeTagLifecycle`, and **`Tables.individuals` must not be raised to `owner`**, which would
   refuse the contributor workflow 11.243 chose. The trap is named in the task so nobody walks back
   into it.
5. **T3 is settled and the preamble was the losing text** — and the part worth keeping is *how* it
   was settled: read from the code, not from either sentence, **and then measured**, with a
   contributor's tombstone of a `Tags` row watched answering `updated` when the rung was reopened on
   purpose. **That is the first server-side test of T3's tombstone route that has ever existed.** A
   contradiction closed by a test rather than by choosing a sentence.
6. **The cross-author loop is derived from `tableMutationRules`, and its exception is read out of
   `_authorizeTagLifecycle`'s source rather than listed** — with the parser throwing rather than
   returning empty, watched by renaming the method and seeing the file fail to load. **That is the
   difference between a check and a check that can quietly cover nothing**, and it is this project's
   oldest defect class. §8 entry 14 is closed.
7. **Item 3's find is the eighteenth instance of the report-not-code class**, and it is worth one
   line rather than a task: §4.7's IN3 cell asserted *"No screen offers a bare
   delete-with-collars-attached"* — inherited from task 11.241's report — **nine days after 11.244
   built exactly that control.** Fixed in this task. **Eighteen is a large number and nothing
   currently catches this shape:** `check_app_quotes` verifies quoted strings, and 11.246's §3.2
   registry verifies that a section exists. **Neither can tell whether a sentence about the code is
   true.** No instrument is proposed here because none is obvious; the count is recorded so that the
   next person who sees a cheap one knows what it is worth.

### Task 11.251, after the first device look — 2026-09-15 — commit 4ad8d3b — Partial

**Michael tested on his phone the same day and found four things; three are fixed here and the
fourth is a hypothesis fixed on the strength of the code, awaiting his second look.**

1. **Both the old and the new collar read "Current" after a swap.** My fault in the first commit:
   I wrote *Current* as "spans today", which is the Record wheel's question, and a collar taken off
   at 14:32 does span today. *Current* now means **not yet recorded as off** — no removed date, or a
   removed time still ahead, or a removed day after today. A date-only removal dated today is not
   current either. Watched red (two "Current" labels), now one.
2. **The newest collar was listed below the older one.** The rows came oldest-first from the
   database and only "current first" was applied. Now: current first, then newest attached first
   (ties on the date break on `created_at`, the same tie-break as everywhere else). Watched red.
3. **The row's three buttons ran off the right edge of the phone.** *Edit attached date*, *Set
   removed date*, *Remove record* were a plain `Row`; overflowed by 394 px at 6.1-inch width in the
   test font (less on the device, but off the edge, as he saw). Now an `OverflowBar` that wraps, and
   the test measures *Remove record* inside the phone's width. **This was live since task 11.248
   added the third button; task 11.166's width sweep predates it.**
4. **The bearing taken on B, before B's collar was swapped, drew grey.** *Hypothesis, from the
   code:* the accepted swap time went through `TimeOfDay`, which has no seconds, so a swap
   confirmed at 14:32:50 was written as 14:32:00 — *earlier than a bearing at 14:32:30*, which then
   fell after the collar left B and before it reached A (a later minute): nobody's, grey. Michael's
   whole test ran inside a few minutes, which is exactly when this bites. **Fixed:** a time accepted
   as offered is written to the second (a time the person *changes* is the minute they picked);
   both screens' tests assert the written instant is not before the moment the link started, and
   both were watched red under the truncation. **I did not have a log capture** — `CLAUDE.md` says
   the log beats the hypothesis — so item 1 for Michael is the measurement.

   the Log.** Michael's words: *"FYI I noticed there is no way to delete a 'no signal' recording

### Tasks 11.248, 11.247 and the two ad-hoc entries — resolved 2026-09-15 by the planning session

**All five entries together, because they are one investigation.** Michael, 2026-09-15: *"I don't
believe sonnet is up to the task. opus or fable might be needed."*

**The investigation is good and it is not being redone.** The third-check entry found the mechanism,
reproduced it in isolation *and* end-to-end through the real write path, correctly identified which
callers are immune and why, and stopped rather than patching. **That is the right shape of a
hand-off** and the new task cites it rather than repeating it.

1. **Task 11.251 is scheduled — Opus, high, fresh window, alone**, and it is above the line. It
   takes the Discovered Scope entry as its measurement and **says why that entry's suggested fix is
   not sufficient on its own**: with a closed interval end, two deployments cover the same 2pm
   bearing on a handover day, and `animalForObservationIn` returns the first match in a list — so
   the widened version would answer **arbitrarily** rather than wrongly-but-findably. **A defect
   with no boundary condition to find it by is worse than the one being fixed.**
2. **The grey bearing is separated out as its own cause, and it is the more serious half.** It is
   not about handovers at all: §5a auto-closes an animal's previous collar whenever a new one is
   attached, and half-open then gives that collar's removal day to no deployment. **Every bearing
   taken on the day a collar comes off is attributed to nobody, today, in every project.** The

### Task 11.247, third check — 2026-09-15 — no commit (investigation only, no code change) — Blocked, needs a new task

**Michael re-checked the colour fix from the entry below and it is still wrong — not the same bug,
a third and deeper one, found and root-caused but deliberately not fixed here. Michael asked that
this go to a fresh task, run by Opus or Fable, rather than be continued in this session.**

**What he saw, in his own words:** animal A yellow, animal B red. Tag 1 on A, tag 2 on B, a
bearing on each. Tag 2 moved from B to A (an ordinary same-day recapture). Afterward on the Map:
the bearing that was always A's turned **grey**, and the bearing that was genuinely B's turned
**yellow** — A's colour, the animal it was never actually on.

**Root cause, confirmed by direct reproduction — not a guess.** `Deployment.covers()`
(`lib/data/models/deployment.dart`) compares a bearing's exact recorded instant against a
same-day removal date the wrong way round: a deployment removed "today" is recorded as ending at
**midnight** today, and a bearing taken at, say, 2pm today is *after* midnight — so `covers()`
says the old deployment does not cover it, and the replacement deployment (which starts at that
same midnight with no end yet) silently claims it instead. Reproduced directly against the
`Deployment` class with no UI involved, and again end-to-end through the real write path
(`DeploymentLinking`, `DeploymentRepository.update`, the same `deploymentDateFor` normalisation
the Animal Detail screen actually uses).

**This is not new, and it is not something today's two fixes could have caught** — they fixed a
different question ("which animal currently owns this collar," a tie on the same date) and never
touched the time-interval question this bug lives in. It has been live since task 11.243/11.244
shipped and affects **three places, not one**: the Log's animal filter (task 11.244), the Map's
animal filter (task 11.247), and the Map's colour/legend (today). A same-day handover — which
§5a/§6 built the whole interlock's one-day tolerance to support as the *ordinary* case — is
exactly the case that trips it, on every one of the three.

Full write-up, including the exact reproduction and a starting-point suggestion for the fix (which
still needs to be checked against the interlock's own day-arithmetic so it doesn't get loosened by
accident), is in `DEVELOPMENT_PLAN.md`'s Discovered Scope, this same date.

**For the planning session:** please draft a new task for this — Michael asked specifically that
it run on **Opus or Fable**, not continue in this Sonnet session, given it's algorithm-correctness
work on a derivation three features depend on. Task 11.247 cannot be marked Done until it lands;
its plan entry says so and names this entry.

1. Nothing to do right now — no code changed in this session's last step, on your explicit
   instruction. The next task will need a device look once it's built, same as this one.

### Ad hoc, follow-up — 2026-09-14 — commit a8cb919 — Done

**Resolves the entry directly below.** Michael answered the three questions: he used the "Set
removed date" control (not the destructive "Remove record"), the second animal already existed,
and force-closing the app did not fix it. That last fact reframed the whole question — it meant
the wrong data was persisted, not merely cached, so the live-refresh investigation in the entry
below was chasing the wrong mechanism.

**Root cause found: a same-day tie in `TagRepository`'s "most recent deployment" join.** A removed
date and a new link on the same calendar day give two deployments the same `attached_date`, and
the join picked which one's animal to name using `MAX(attached_date)` with a SQLite bare column —
a guarantee that says nothing about which row wins a tie. Reproduced deterministically: the tie
always broke toward the *older* deployment, exactly Michael's symptom, and it affected every
reader of that join, not only the Record screen's wheel — the Map's legend from task 11.247 reads
the same field. `DeploymentRepository.latestAnimalForTag` had the identical defect in its own
Dart-side walk. Both fixed to break the tie by `created_at` (a real instant) rather than a
calendar day or a random UUID; no window function, per `schema.dart`'s existing note that a
runtime query cannot assume `ROW_NUMBER()` on every bundled SQLite. Full write-up, including why
the day's first two hypotheses were wrong, in `DEVELOPMENT_PLAN.md`'s Discovered Scope.

`flutter test`: 3277 passed, 0 failed, 15 skipped (one new test, watched red against the pre-fix
code before the fix was restored). `flutter analyze`: clean.

**For the planning session:** nothing — this is a bug fix with its own regression test, not a
scope question.

### Task 11.243 — acted on 2026-09-14 by the planning session; **Partial until the redeploy**

**Built, and the two defects it found on the way are worth more than the feature.** Both were visible
only because its migration tests run on **populated** databases: an idempotence check that read a
column a *later* migration deletes, so the step ran twice and minted a duplicate animal; and deferred
foreign keys making `DELETE` and `ALTER TABLE … DROP COLUMN` incompatible inside one transaction.
**On an empty database neither statement has anything to trip over and the migration passes.**
**Second time deferred constraints have bitten this project** — 11.227 hit the same wall from the
other side — **and both times the fixture with rows in it is what found it.** Now a rule in
`CLAUDE.md`: a migration test seeds every table the migration touches, or it is a syntax check
wearing a test's clothes.

**The document was wrong and the task said so, which is the behaviour the brief asked for.** §5
claimed `unknown` was an addition; `IndividualStatus` has carried it since v16, so §5 needed no code.
**Corrected in the document, and the claim is now asserted by a test** — a sentence in a document
that nothing checks is the next thing to go stale.

**Its four judgement calls are accepted, and the third produced a task.** `Tag_Library` wiped too;
*"whose collar is this"* and *"which animal was this bearing about"* kept as separate methods with
different answers (a collar off Marie in June is still listed under Marie, and its bearings since are
attributed to nobody — that distinction is right and easy to lose); the archive's v16→v17 crossing
deliberately lossy with `_lowestMigratableMajor`'s *lossless* contract **amended rather than quietly
broken.**

> **The third call moved a permission rung: linking is contributor-level, where `Tags.individual_id`
> was owner-only.** The reasoning is good — *"which collar went on which bird is what the person
> holding the bird knows"* — **but `PERMISSIONS_MATRIX.md` has no `Deployments` row, and nothing
> checks that it should.** That document opens with *"nothing below is filled from memory."* **A
> hand-maintained list, inside the document whose whole purpose is to stop a permission drifting
> unnoticed** — which is finding N-1's own shape. **Task 11.246**: the row, derived from the code,
> plus a test that fails when any synced table has no section. **`Individuals` is probably missing
> too; if it is, that is the finding rather than a second chore.**

**Three things went to 11.244**: two methods deliberately left uncalled (`animalForObservation`,
`unlink`) whose uncalled-method test **goes red the day 11.244 lands, which is the design working**;
§5a's missing half, **with a warning written into the entry that the interlock's refusal will read as
a bug until then**; and the now-unread `TagLibraryEntry.color_hex` — **decided: offer it as the new
animal's starting colour, or take the swatch off; a swatch showing a colour nothing uses is the one
outcome not allowed.**

**`/11-56` already carries `Deployments`** — added 2026-09-14 in the queue sweep, before this task
asked for it.

**The server half is done, 2026-09-14, and the log line is what the brief asked for.** The beta
server ran **v15 → v16 → v17** in one start and said so:

```
schema v16: 4 tag row(s) found; 4 individual(s) created, one per tag, none merged by name
schema v17: … THIS MIGRATION DELETED DATA ON PURPOSE (ANIMALS_AND_DEPLOYMENTS_DESIGN.md section 9):
            19 row(s) destroyed … Projects, memberships and sign-in are untouched.
```

**A destructive step that names its count, cites the decision that authorised it, and says what
survived** — the requirement written into the brief, met in the one place it matters.

**And the sequence is worth reading.** v16 created four animals one-per-tag and v17 destroyed them
minutes later. **That is correct:** 11.243 removed the backfill *going forward* and did not rewrite a
shipped migration, which would have broken the reconstruction tests that make the chain trustworthy.
**The chain stayed honest at the cost of a few seconds of pointless work, which is the right trade.**

**DONE 2026-09-14.** Michael rebuilt the phone and it works. **Server first was the rule and it was
followed, on both halves.**

### Task 11.241 — 2026-09-13 — commit dbc059b (no code since) — Partial, and Michael asks for a rescope
**Michael did the device look, and then reviewed the design, and the design is wrong in a way the
planning session should re-scope rather than this task patch.** No code was changed after his
review; this entry is the record. His words, and his answers to my questions, are below so nothing
here is my paraphrase of a decision.

**What he saw on the phone.** *"I checked and the merge with the same animal as function work."*
Project Setup shows two animals, one of which has two tags because he merged two animals. So the
merge, the counts and the grouping all render; that half of the device check is done.

**His concern, in his words:** *"I'm not sure why you called the animals list 'tags' in the project
setup screen and why you put that animal list behind the project setup screen when all the other
items (logs, tag database, etc.) are exposed on the main more list. Seems like the animal's list
should be on that menu as well. Also that menu has an 'add tag' button, but shouldn't that be an
'add animal' button? And when I click on the animal, it takes me to a screen that looks like the old
'tag details' screen ... but there is no way to see, add, or remove, a tag from the animal record on
that screen. In the tag database, the tags are still listed with a tag/animal name. That should
probably get updated to a Tag Identifier/ID so that there isn't any confusion that a tag identifier
and an animal name are different."*

**The workflow he expects, in his words:** *"create a project, add a listing of all the tags they
purchased, then build a list of individuals either all at once if they have a population of
existing animals, or one at a time as they capture individuals. Only after they add the animals in
their list would they link a tag to an animal in the app. If it was a recapture of an existing tagged
animal, they could update the remove date of the tag already linked to that animal and then link a
new tag to the animal with an updated attached date."*

**Why the built thing disagrees with that, stated so the rescope starts from the right place.**
11.240 and 11.241 built animals as *derived from collars*: every tag creation makes an animal named
after the tag (`TagRepository.insert`'s `createIndividual: true` default; the v16 migration did the
same to every existing tag), and the animals list was a regrouping of the project's tag list. Under
Michael's model **tags are equipment bought first, animals are the subjects, and linking is a
deliberate, dated act** — so a tag with no animal is the normal starting state, not an exception to
list last, and "add tag" must never invent an animal. That is a change to a decision 11.240 made on
purpose, which is why it is the planning session's to make.

**His answers to the five questions I asked, verbatim where it matters:**
1. *Which "add tag" button:* the one on **Project Setup**. *"I want the add tags to live primarily in
   the tags database manager."*
2. *Attached/removed dates and a schema major bump:* *"Its okay if we have a schema major update. I
   don't have real data yet, just test data. I only have one version of the app on my phone. It is
   okay to make the tag put on date and tag off dates empty."* — i.e. `Tags.date_put_on` becomes
   nullable, which under `wire_shape_freeze.dart` is **schema major 5**, and he has accepted that
   cost (one rebuild of one phone).
3. *The Record screen's tag wheel:* *"It should be the same as it is today"* — and the rule that makes
   that safe: *"always show the tag with the currently attached date for the animal. Also put an
   interlock on the animal such that it can't have two tags linked to it unless the tags
   attached/removed dates don't overlap by more than one day (old tags are replaced by new tags on
   the same day). A tag can only have one [animal] that is currently on it per the tag dates. If a
   user tries to link a tag to an animal with dates that overlap by more than one day it tells the
   user to fix the removed/attached dates of the tags."*
4. *Bulk animals:* *"we'll want a csv import eventually but we'll do that later."*
5. *Count on his phone:* two animals, one with two tags (the merged pair). Test data only.

**What changed, in one sentence:** a project's collars are now listed under the animals that wore
them, a person can say two animals are one (and the merge provably moves no bearings), the Log and

package and server untouched by this task) and every claim below is asserted — but nobody has opened

**Decisions this task made, so they are not re-derived:**
- **The animals list is on Project Setup, not the "Tag Database" screen the brief named.** That
  screen has been the device's personal library since task 11.219 — transmitters in no project, which
  by the model have no animal. Animals belong to a project, so they are listed where the project's
  collars are.
- **A collar with no animal goes last, under "Collars with no animal", with an Assign button.** Last
  because it is the exception; under a heading so it is never read as the animal above's; with the
  button because that row is where the person who can answer will find it.
- **The merge direction:** you open the duplicate and pick the animal it really is; the one you pick
  survives. The confirmation names what moves, what stays and what cannot be undone (the absorbed
  animal's own record). Owner-only, because re-pointing collars is a change to existing tags.
- **The track across collars is not drawn.** Filtering the map by the animal shows every collar's
  bearings and estimates in her colour, and the Log filtered by her, in time order, *is* the track. A
  line joining two transmitters' estimates would draw a path nobody measured.
- **Recording: the wheel still picks a collar; the animal's name is appended in brackets only when it
  differs from the collar's.** Every collar named after its animal — all of them until somebody merges
  or renames — reads exactly as before, and the fold is measured unchanged either way.
- **The library keeps its colour, as a documented seed.** Written on `TagLibraryEntry.colorHex` and
  pinned by a test: the animal a copied collar creates starts in it, and changing it afterwards
  recolours nothing anywhere.
- **The export zip's entry names are undated** (`observations.csv`, `non_detections.csv`,
  `truth_points.csv`, `tags.csv`, `individuals.csv`) so a script can name them; the archive is
  `<project>_csv_<date>.zip`. Only the packaging changed.

### Task 10.87 — resolved 2026-09-13 by the planning session

**Done, and the re-scoping was right — but the premise I re-scoped it on was measured false, and
that is the entry's main content.** My bullet said a project not yet on this device *"cannot be
overwritten, so the list must not appear at all."* **True of the project's records. False of
people.** `Users` and `User_Emails` are **global**, so a file that renames somebody this device
already knows — Michael, or a teammate from an unrelated project — reaches the consent gate on a
first-time import. Watched happening on `Users.last_name`. The dialog stays for that case and says
so in one sentence.

> **The error was scoping a claim about "an import" to the part of an import that is
> project-scoped** — and it is **the second inference-from-a-neighbouring-fact of mine in two
> days**, after 11.237's "the edits reach the server and are refused" (they never left the device).
> Both were reasoned from something true standing next to the question. **Corrected in both places,
> including 11.237's table, where none of the four cells means "no consent needed".**

**What shipped is the right shape.** *"Bearings · 1000 records, 1000 values replaced, 12 records
removed: latitude, longitude"* is a summary a person can actually read, and the Sync Status screen
shows **one card per import or sync rather than one per record** — which is the finding 11.24
originally raised, fixed at the class rather than on a third named screen.

**Michael confirmed it on his phone, 2026-09-13** — he imported a backup of a project already on the
device and the dialog read as a summary he would actually read. **That look was not required by the
acceptance**; the task offered it as *"two minutes, worth it"*, and it is the only evidence that
exists for the half of this task that is a judgement about legibility. **A suite cannot tell you a
summary is readable**, so the optional look was the real acceptance for that half and is recorded as
such.

**The class is closed at five: four fixed, one accepted with a trigger.** The import receipt's
refusal list keeps its first-20-in-declaration-order cut. **Accepted, and the task's own reasoning is
what settles it: a refusal is the file *failing* to write**, so a padded list hides *that the file
tried something*, never a change to the person's data — and nothing today asks anybody to act on that
list. **The trigger is written into the entry: the moment any flow asks a person to act on it, this
becomes a task**, because then the file is choosing what the person acts on, which is L-5 exactly.
**Four fixed and one accepted with a named condition is a closed class, not a loose end.**

**The reasoned-not-measured finding gets a number and a first step: task 11.239.** A v13 archive of a
project whose collar was later forked on the importing device may land as **two tags for one
animal** — the archive's row keyed `(t1, B)`, the device's fork keyed `(t2, B)` with `lineage_id =
t1`, and nothing making them the same row. **10.87 was right to reason it and right to stop.** The
brief's first step is a database test, and **it says in so many words that one tag is a clean
negative and ends the task** — a result, not something to pad into a change. **Ranked below the line
provisionally, with the ranking to be re-decided on the measured answer**: if it reproduces it is a
duplicate collar in a scientific record, reachable on Michael's own device, and that is an
above-the-line argument the task should make rather than inherit.

**And `SchemaMigrator`'s v14 comment gets fixed either way.** It says the fork *"cannot arise in an
archive at all"* — **true of the archive alone, false of the archive meeting a forked device.**
Correct when written, falsified by a change one file over; the most-repeated shape in this project's
catalogue and the reason 11.239 exists at all.

**Copy is in `WEBSITE_PLAN.md`**, with the people-are-global sentence flagged, because a guide line
saying a first-time import changes nothing would now be wrong. **`markSyncConflictReviewed` is left
in place** — one line, wrapped by the event version; it goes if the uncalled-method guard ever
objects, which is a cheaper trigger than deciding now.

## Open — waiting on Michael

### Added 2026-09-18 — go back to NAU about what the liability text is for

**Task 11.285 is blocked on this and nothing else.** The two paragraphs from the AVP for Research
and Innovation are boilerplate from a **two-party patent license**: *THE PARTIES*, *THIS AGREEMENT*,
*LICENSOR*, *LICENSEE*, *LICENSED PRODUCTS*, *PATENT RIGHTS*, and a liability cap of *“the amounts
paid by Licensee to Licensor under this Agreement.”*

**Somebody who installs TriTrack has signed no agreement and paid nothing.** The cap evaluates to
zero for them — probably the intent, but expressed as a reference to a document they have never
seen, and the warranty disclaimer is about whether a patent issues rather than whether the app works.

**The question to ask him:** *is this meant for end users, or for an agreement with somebody
licensing the technology?* His *“feel free to adapt as needed”* suggests he knows it needs shaping.
**You may need both documents.**

**And the sentence this app needs is not in what he sent.** The risk here is not patent validity —
it is that a position estimate is an estimate, computed from bearings somebody typed and from
third-party elevation data, and a crew may make a navigation decision from it. **Task 11.285's entry
carries a starting point for counsel to rewrite**; it is not legal advice and was not written by a
lawyer.

**Nothing ships until the wording is settled.** Release checklist **F7** is the backstop.

### Added 2026-09-18 — a decision only you can make: does the guide belong inside the app?

**Task 11.286 item 1 adds a row that opens the guide in a browser. Item 2 is this, and it is not a
task.** The guide is a website; TriTrack is an offline-first field app. **A link solves “I am at my
desk” and does nothing for a crew in a canyon**, which is where somebody actually needs to know what
*contested* means.

**The argument that a link is enough:** the app already explains itself at the point of need — Sync
Status carries the sentence, a held row carries its own remedy, the interlock names the two dates.
**The guide is for learning, not for rescue.**

**Three options with their real costs**, in task 11.286's entry: link only (free; no guide with no
signal), bundle text-only (~11,200 words, small, **loses all 117 screenshots and five diagrams**),
bundle the whole thing for one phone profile (biggest download, and **a second copy that can fall out
of step with the site** — the hazard this project fears most).

**The trigger:** the first beta crew who says they wanted the guide and could not get it. Until then
the link is the cheap answer.

### ~~Added 2026-09-16 — the original sequence~~

**Michael, 2026-09-16:** *"I can't do this until I get home and can run the VM server when I'm not
on the university network."* **This is the sequence, kept here so it survives the conversation.**

**Rebuild the phone and redeploy the server together** — `git pull` on the VM, then
`scripts/server_up.sh --build`. **The server change is what makes a swap sync at all**, and without
it half the steps below fail for the wrong reason.

> **Do not pick 5:00 pm exactly for any time in this test.** A swap timed at 17:00:00 Arizona reads
> as UTC midnight on the server and is refused — real, rare, recorded (§4a's cross-zone trigger) —
> and it would look like a bug today.

1. **Count the legacy pairs first, before changing anything.** Open Record and count animals showing
   two collars on the wheel. Each is an old same-day swap recorded as two bare days. **Report the
   number** — it decides whether repairing them is worth a task or whether a wipe (§9) is simpler.
2. **The prompt should be gone.** An animal with two collars shows **no line above the wheel** — no
   *"set a removal time?"*, no chooser. That is task 11.263's deletion.
3. **Sync Status.** Anything held as *"the server would not take this"* from a swap made since
   2026-09-14 should go through on retry. **Say whether the held count drops to zero.** That is the
   server defect nobody had ever exercised.
4. **The ordinary swap, end to end — the main event.** Collar 1 off Kea (*Edit removed date* → today
   → *Set a time*), then link collar 2 to Kea. Expect: the confirmation offers a time; the wheel
   shows **one** collar for Kea; the Map colours the morning's bearing as Kea's; **and it syncs.**
5. **The refusal.** Create the overlap deliberately — a bare-day removal of *today* on a collar where
   another already covers part of today. Expect the interlock's sentence naming the dates to fix,
   **never a silent adjustment.**
6. **The narrowed *Day only*.** *Edit removed date* → today. **When another collar covers part of
   today**: only *Set a time* and *Cancel*, with *"Another collar already covers part of today, so
   this one needs a time — the moment it came off."* Otherwise the three buttons as before.

**And one decision is open, with the planning session's recommendation:** *Day only* is currently
withheld only where it would overlap **right now**. A bare-day removal recorded this morning, when
nothing overlapped yet, **makes that collar unlinkable to anyone for the rest of the day, and the
other animal's picker hides it without saying why** — Michael's own tag-2 flow of 2026-09-15, and a
silently missing option is this project's worst shape. **Recommended: withhold *Day only* for today
entirely** — the time is defaulted to now, one tap — **and keep it for a past day**, where a time
would be invented.

### Added 2026-09-12 — one `chown` on the Ubuntu VM

`scripts/server_up.sh` warned that `.dev_magic_links` is owned by **root** while the server runs as
uid 1000, so the development magic-link sender could not write a sign-in link into it — and
`/auth/magic-link` answers `202` either way (§4.5), so the link would simply never appear. **It is
not biting today** (that sender belongs to the `dev-lan` overlay, which the beta host does not use),
but the directory will stay wrong until somebody fixes it. On the VM, in `~/repos/tritrack`:

```
sudo chown -R 1000:1000 .dev_magic_links
```

**It got that owner the same way the backups did** — a raw `docker compose up`, which makes Docker
create a missing bind-mount directory as root. **Two faults, one cause, one habit.** Use
`scripts/server_up.sh` to raise that stack from now on; it is what knows who you are.

```
schema v12: applied

```

discards; without that change the upgrade would have done the right thing invisibly.

### ~~Added 2026-09-11 — one manual gate run around 20 September~~ — CANCELLED 2026-09-11, and 1 October is now THREE edits

**The mid-month manual run is off: Michael ran out of GitHub Actions minutes on 2026-09-11**, so
there are none to spend on it. The reminder that was set for 20 September has been removed rather
than left to fire and ask for something impossible.

> **What this means, stated plainly, because it is the more important half: there is no CI at all
> until 1 October.** Every push from now until then runs nothing — the budget is spent and "stop at
> the limit" is set. **Pushing is still safe and still worth doing** (it is how the code reaches the
> VM and how it stops living on one laptop); it simply buys no verification.
>
> **So every task landing this month has local runs as its only evidence**, and the two commands that
> cover what the pre-commit hook does not — `scripts/run_server_tests_docker.sh` and
> `scripts/gate_smoke_test.sh` — stop being a good habit and become the whole of it. Task briefs from
> here to 1 October say so.
>
> **And one thing to carry knowingly:** work merged in this window has never been built or tested on
> anything but Michael's Mac. The first push after 1 October will be the first time this month's code
> meets a clean Linux checkout, and it should be treated as a real event rather than a formality.

**On 1 October, reopening the nightly is TWO edits in one file**, not one: uncomment the `schedule:`
block in `.github/workflows/gate-instruments.yml` **and** put `github.event_name == 'schedule' ||`
back at the front of the self-test step's `if:`. Both spots carry a comment saying so, and
`server/test/security/shipped_defaults_test.dart` goes red if only the first is made — run
`scripts/run_server_tests_docker.sh` afterwards and it will tell you.

**Added 2026-09-17 — the third edit, in a different file: give the suite a daylight-saving zone.**
Tasks 11.276 and 11.277 were two timezone defects that lived on `main` for weeks. Neither was a hole
in the instruments: `offline-suite.yml` runs the full Flutter suite on `ubuntu-latest`, which is UTC,
so **CI would have caught both on the push that introduced them** — it was simply switched off.
**What CI still will not see is a zone that observes daylight saving.** Arizona does not. UTC does
not. So this project has never run its suite in a DST zone at all, and a crew in one is an ordinary
thing, not an exotic one.

- **Add one DST leg to `offline-suite.yml`** — `TZ: America/New_York` or `Pacific/Auckland` (the
  second is also the southern-hemisphere, other-side-of-the-dateline case `deploymentDateFor`'s own
  comment is written about, so it is the better of the two).
- **On the nightly only, not on every push.** A second full suite on every push doubles the offline
  suite's minutes against a $0 budget; the nightly is where rot-that-nobody-touched belongs, and
  that is exactly what a DST transition is — a defect that appears twice a year without a commit.
  **Michael's call if he would rather spend the minutes per-push; the recommendation is nightly.**
- **Say in the file why that zone and not another**, or the next person deletes it as arbitrary.

### Added 2026-09-10 — a one-page architecture diagram for the ITS letter, and one thing to decide

**`CLAUDE_DOCS/TriTrack-server-architecture.pdf`** — one page, written for a system administrator:

from `docker-compose.yml` + `docker-compose.tls.yml`, not from the letter's prose.
**`TriTrack-server-architecture.html` beside it is the source**; it prints back to the same PDF from
any browser, so it can be regenerated when the stack changes.

**Two documents were corrected on the way, and both were right when written.** The ITS letter said
**four** containers — true on 2026-08-31, and **task 11.79 added the audit-retention service the next
day**. The deployment primer said **three services** — true before tasks 10.49, 11.78 and 11.79 each
added one. Both now say five, and both point at the diagram.

**One thing for you to decide, because it will be asked.** The `server` container's image declares no
`USER`, so the process runs as root **inside its own container** — the ordinary Flutter/Dart server
image default, and not the same thing as root on the host. The backup containers do declare a user
(`postgres`, uid 70). An information-security reviewer may well ask about it. **Options: leave it and
answer the question if it comes; or add a non-root `USER` to `server/Dockerfile` before sending,
which is a small task and a better answer.** Say which and it becomes one.
