**Resolved by the planning session, 2026-08-29 — both entries together.**

1. **Automatic sync and the frequency control are task 11.59**, with a command file,

### Task 11.54 field report — 2026-08-29 — commit a6bea69 (unchanged) — NEW TASK REQUESTED

**Michael ran two more rounds on real hardware after `a6bea69` was pushed and hit
four things. He asked for a task rather than a fix, and no code was changed for
this entry — nothing below was reproduced by this session.** Everything marked
*measured* is read out of the code; everything marked *hypothesis* is a candidate
the task should test, not a finding.

**Round A — the project he had left and deleted on 2026-08-29.** The Mac issued a
fresh invite code. Entering it on the iPhone was refused with *"You're already on
that project. If it isn't on this device yet, use 'Join a project' instead — you
don't need a code."* The project does not appear under "Join a project" either.

**Round B — a clean run on a brand-new project.** Create on the Mac, join on the
iPhone, leave on the iPhone, delete on the iPhone. **The Mac never registered the
departure — it still shows him as a current member.** A second invite code was
then refused on the iPhone as "already a member", while the project is still not
visible there.

**For the planning session**

1. **Open a task for the whole cycle: add → invite → join → leave → remove →
   delete → re-invite → rejoin, on two devices, every ordering.** The four
   symptoms above came out of running two orderings once each. The pattern this
   task keeps producing is that each ordering is fine in isolation and the
   *transitions* are not, so the acceptance should be the matrix, not the four
   bugs. **Both directions of removal belong in it** — the person leaving, and an
   owner removing them — because only the first has ever been walked.

2. **Correct something I got wrong yesterday, in this file, with confidence.** The
   entry below says `ProjectDirectoryClient.listAvailableToJoin` treating a
   tombstoned local project as "already have it" is *"currently unreachable —
   nobody can reach it today"*. **Michael reached it the same day.** It is the
   whole of round A's dead end and it is measured, not hypothesised:
   `listAvailableToJoin` queries `Projects` with no `deleted_at` filter, so a
   tombstoned row counts as present and the project is excluded from the list.
   Combined with the server correctly refusing the code (he *is* a member there,
   from the successful redemption on 2026-08-29), **there is no route back to that
   project on that device.** The task must fix the exclusion; a prediction offered
   as a finding is the mistake this project has now recorded three times, and this
   one is mine.

3. **The "already a member" message gives advice that does not work.** *"Use 'Join
   a project' instead"* is only good advice if the project is listed there, and
   item 2 is exactly when it is not. This is the same shape as task 11.54's own
   subject — a surface naming a remedy the app cannot deliver — so the task should
   treat the message and the listing as one fix, not two.

4. **Round B's departure never reaching the Mac is the sharpest item, and it is
   new.** On 2026-08-29 a departure *did* propagate — the Mac showed him as a past
   member, which was one of the three checks that passed. So something differs
   between the two runs. What I measured, and what I did not:

   - **Measured, and it rules a candidate out:** the leaver's own departure row
     *is* offered to the server. `Project_Memberships` is one of the four tables
     `offer_rules.dart` withholds, but it withholds only rows naming *somebody
     else* — `userColumns` is `['user_id', last_modified_by]`, and on a departure
     both name the caller. So "the device never sends it" is not the explanation.
   - **Hypothesis, and the one I would test first:** the server accepts a
     non-owner's membership write only when it is a *departure* under
     `membership_departure.dart`, which requires every column but `end_date`,
     `updated_at`, `revision`, `last_modified_by` and `origin_device_id` to be
     **byte-identical to the stored row**. In round B that row was **written by
     the server** when the invitation was redeemed; in the 2026-08-29 run it may
     not have been. If the iPhone's copy differs in any immutable column, the
     departure is refused and held — invisibly, because he then deleted the
     project and the held-row warning lives on that project's sync screen.
   - **Measured, and it is a dead end regardless of the cause:** if a departure
     is *not* confirmed by the server, `MembershipController.leaveProject` leaves
     the project **linked** and the row pending. `SyncController.syncNow` and
     `syncIfDue` both operate on the **active** project only. A deleted project is
     never the active one. **So a departure that fails to go out on the way out
     has no route out afterwards, ever.** That is true today independent of round
     B's cause, and it is worth its own acceptance line.
   - **Not ruled out and not investigated:** that the departure did reach the
     server and the Mac simply never showed it. That is task 11.41's shape — rows
     stuck on the owner's device — and the task should check the server's own
     table before blaming either client.

5. **Sequencing note.** Items 2 and 3 are small and independent; item 4 is the one
   that needs the two-device stack. If the task is split, split it there rather
   than by symptom.

**For Michael**

1. **Nothing to do for git** — no code changed for this entry; `a6bea69` is what
   you pushed and it stands.
2. **A risk you are carrying right now, and it is small but real: your iPhone has
   at least one project it cannot get back.** It is a member of it on the server,
   holds a hidden copy of it locally, and neither the code nor the "Join a
   project" list will let it in. Nothing is lost — the project and its synced
   records are safe on the Mac and on the server — but that device is stuck on
   those projects until the task above lands.
3. **If you want it unstuck sooner, deleting and reinstalling the iPhone app would
   do it** — it clears the local copy, after which "Join a project" would list the
   project again. **It also destroys anything on that phone that never synced**, so
   check the phone's sync screen first, and I would rather you waited than did this
   in a hurry. Say the word if you want me to look for a gentler route.
4. **When you next run round B, note one thing for the task:** on the iPhone, open
   More → Sync Status *immediately after leaving and before deleting*, and say
   whether anything appears under "Waiting to sync". That single observation

Ran items 1–4 of the merged running order in full. Item 5 (the sync bookmark's
server identity) is **reproduced and measured but not fixed** — it needs a

**For the planning session**

1. **Give task 11.51's remaining half a new task number.** 11.54 built the
   classification 11.51 asked to join and **deliberately did not add a cause for
   "my bookmark belongs to a different server", because nothing in the protocol
   can produce one** — an unreachable state in a classification reads as covered.
   The mechanism is reproduced in `test/data/sync/stale_cursor_new_server_test.dart`.
   The new task needs: the server minting a database identifier once at schema

   the sync status screen; and the missing `SyncFailureCause` value. Full entry is
   in Phase 11's Discovered Scope.
2. **The reproduction found something the original reading did not name, and it is
   worse than the cursor.** Row receipts are deliberately kept when a project
   unlinks, on the stated grounds that "a receipt is a statement about what the
   server holds, which does not stop being true." That reasoning does not survive
   the server changing underneath it — it is a statement about *which* server holds
   it. A receipt from the old database keeps a local row off the new server's push
   set, and unlike the cursor it never self-heals. Whatever task takes item 1 must
   clear receipts too, not just the cursor.
3. **Task 11.53 item 1 is not a snackbar, and task 11.42's sweep is not
   implicated.** The persistent grey bar is `SyncStatusBanner`
   (`lib/routing/app_router.dart:257`), which task 10.12 specified as never hiding
   itself while sync is available. It reports the truth. No sixth `persist: false`
   was needed and no guard is warranted. Whether it *should* be permanently visible
   is Michael's decision — item 2 in his list below — and reversing it would be a
   task, because it reverses a decision 10.12 made with a stated reason.
4. **Task 11.53 item 2's premise needs a screenshot before it can be a task.** The
   app declares 22 plain `AppBar`s, no `AppBarTheme`, and no `titleTextStyle`
   anywhere, so every screen title resolves to one shared style — 18px at weight
   800, in `lib/core/theme/app_theme.dart`. **"More" therefore cannot be larger
   than any other screen's header.** Either all of them look large (that shared
   style plus iOS Dynamic Type, a decision to accept or change) or one does (which
   contradicts the code and is the more interesting answer).
5. **Add the rejoin-after-delete case to whichever task next touches joining a
   project.** 11.54 made a departed member's copy deletable through the existing
   soft-delete path. The tombstone cannot reach anybody else — `offer_rules.dart`
   already classifies `Projects` among the tables a device never offers the server
   — but **nothing established what happens if that person rejoins afterwards**:
   the local tombstone carries a newer `updated_at` than the server's copy, so the
   rejoined project may come back invisible on that device. Not fixed because
   reaching it needs a live server and a rejoin, which this task could not run.
6. **The walkthrough still has no stable server address, and 11.54 did not add
   one.** Task 11.51's spec asked for an mDNS `.local` hostname or a fixed router
   lease. `./scripts/dev_lan_address.sh` already removes the *retyping* (task
   11.37); what remains needs the specific answer to "is a `.local` hostname
   reachable from the app on iOS, given the local-network permission and the
   cleartext exemption," which this session could not test and did not guess at.
   Task 11.40's capability sweep is the natural home for the general question.
7. **A behaviour change worth knowing about, in an existing test.** A creator who
   transferred a project away is now offered the Delete control, because they are a
   past member of it. `test/features/more/projects_screen_test.dart` asserted the
   opposite and was updated with the reason. 11.1's ownership rule is untouched —
   this is 11.54's departed-member rule also applying to them.

**For Michael**

2. **A decision only you can make: should the grey sync bar hide itself when
